comments.author: virtuallynathan
comments.story: A beginner's guide to intermittent fasting (2012)
comments.why: Calorie labeling accuracy questioned; counting is not very helpful
comments.text: Do you know how many calories you burn? Do you actually know how many calories are in your food? I have a metabolic cart, and the answer surprises me sometimes on the former - just standing at my desk all day I burn >3300kcal. I actually went to talk to the guy in the Casey Neistat video about food labels, and almost bought a bomb calorimeter. Calorie counting, while not useless, is not very helpful. [VIDEO]

comments.author: thesimon
comments.story: How do food manufacturers calculate the calorie count of packaged foods? (2003)
comments.why: Calorie labels in the US can be inaccurate, plus restaurant counts
comments.text: And apparently in the US you can be off by whatever you want [VIDEO] The video also deals with calorie count in restaurants. The NYC regulation to require calorie counts directly on the menu really seems like a good idea. Other than the people already knowing the rough calorie count, who checks the obscure and difficult tables on the website?
